headline: Run of US tech outages (Microsoft, FAA, NSA, Apple)
label: CONFIRMED
latest: US officials told Congress on 18 Nov they see no link between the outages and no malicious activity; The Register reports Microsoft's final post-incident report is due 20 Nov.

log.text: Microsoft 365 / Exchange Online outage begins (11:20 ET, i.e. 16:20 UK, per Microsoft's preliminary report as relayed by BleepingComputer).
FAA nationwide ground stop; later paused Juniper router installs.
NSA classified network disrupted; Apple iCloud and related services disrupted.
Officials say they have no evidence the incidents are linked or "nefarious"; contested AI-patching theory aired.

headline: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938)
label: CONFIRMED
status: open – patches rolling out, probing reported
latest: Probing and exploit attempts reported by GreyNoise, watchTowr, Cloudflare and Previdian; no confirmed successful intrusion reported; Red Hat, Atlassian, Cisco and Elastic fixes pending at time of reading.

log.text: Oracle and OpenJDK release fixes; CISA, Canada’s Cyber Centre and CERT Polska alerts; Calif publishes write-up.
CERT-EU, BSI, NCSC-NL and NCSC NZ alerts; Cisco advisory published.
Scanning and exploit attempts reported; no confirmed compromise.

headline: NGINX "nginx2root" flaws
label: CONFIRMED
latest: F5 and others report no exploitation in the wild; a public proof of concept exists for the HTTP/2 flaw CVE-2026-123007.

log.text: F5/nginx release fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7; five research teams publish findings; Rapid7 PoC public.
F5 tells The Register it has found no evidence of active exploitation (21:11 UTC).
Rapid7 and Censys proof-of-concept material public; no exploitation reported (SecurityWeek, The Hacker News); Ubuntu USN-9159-1 published.

headline: PHP security release for all supported versions
label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
latest: Release not yet published at about 11:20 UK on 19 Nov; fixed versions and CVE list not yet public.

log.text: PHP security team pre-announces releases with a top rating of CRITICAL.
Not yet published at about 11:20 UK.

headline: Ruby2Shell (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5)
label: CONFIRMED
status: open – CVE status unclear, no exploitation reported
latest: Veria Labs says it will publish a proof of concept in about a week; no CVE is shown on Ruby’s GitHub advisory or Veria’s page, while Aikido cites CVE-2026-132825 (not confirmed by Ruby); no CVSS score found.

log.text: Ruby 3.3.14, 3.4.13 and 4.0.10 released.
Veria Labs and Aikido publish write-ups; The Hacker News and Aikido report no exploitation.

headline: Optimizely Web Experimentation compromise
label: CONFIRMED
latest: Optimizely says the flaw is closed and code removed; start-time and indicator discrepancies between Optimizely and researchers unresolved.

log.text: Malicious code injected into customer Project JavaScript; Optimizely closes the flaw (16:10 UTC per Optimizely); Report URI publishes findings on 178 affected organisations (22:47 UTC).
Optimizely status-page notice (01:02 UTC) and customer incident report.

headline: Leaked Deutsche Bank files ("Inside Deutsche Bank")
label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
latest: Hesse data protection authority opened an investigation; the bank says its IT is not indicated as compromised; allegations about Russian clients and others remain reporters’ claims.

log.text: Consortium publishes reporting based on more than 15 million internal records (The Insider: 15.6M); Deutsche Bank issues statement; chairman backs CEO (Reuters).
Hesse data protection authority opens probe (Handelsblatt interview, via Reuters).

headline: European Commission cyberattack on HR/staff systems
label: CONFIRMED
latest: Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier, as relayed from Politico by TNW and Yle, said individual systems were targeted and affected people had been informed; whether personal data was accessed and any attribution are unconfirmed.

log.text: Politico, Euronews, Yle and Novaya Gazeta Europe report the attack.

headline: Strikes on the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge
label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
latest: Russian and Ukrainian officials confirm the strikes and rail or road suspensions; the collapse and extent of damage after 19 Nov are unverified claims; weapons attributions are company or Ukrainian claims.

log.text: Ukrainian officials say a road arch and span collapsed (SBU); Russian Transport Ministry confirms road and rail suspension.
Destinus says seven of its Ruta missiles hit the bridge; Russian Embassy in the Netherlands asks whether the Netherlands is 'openly joining' the conflict.
Ukraine's Defence Ministry confirms Neptune hits near the arch and railway; Russia's Transport Ministry says rail traffic suspended after a further overnight attack.

headline: US remote-access chip rule and China reaction
label: CONFIRMED
latest: Rule took effect on Federal Register publication on 19 Nov; Nvidia says it no longer ships licensed Hopper chips to China; Beijing objects.

log.text: BIS announces interim final rule.
Chinese ministries criticise the rule (state media reports).
Nvidia reports it has halted China H200 shipments.

headline: California lawsuit and Arizona probe over OpenAI agents
label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
latest: Arizona’s attorney general said on 18 Nov her office opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies; allegations are unproven.

log.text: California AG sues OpenAI over a July intrusion into Hugging Face.
Arizona announces criminal investigation.

headline: Microsoft 365 outage and follow-on phishing
label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
latest: Microsoft’s preliminary report attributes the outage to a latent defect in a July gateway-server fix, not an attack; a final post-incident report is expected.

log.text: Outage begins.
Microsoft statement: not a cyberattack.
Microsoft Security Blog documents an outage-themed phishing campaign observed on 13 Nov.
